NEW YORK, FRIDAY MORNlNG.—Despatches received here report that B,MO insurgents have b,sen landed with- in 20 miles of Valparaiso. The Government are com- pletely surprised, as•they expected an attack upon Co- quimbo. An important battle in the neighbourhood of Valparaiso is believed to be imminent.

Official despatches received in Paris on -Thursday con- Erm the news of the terrible cyclone which has visited the French possessionof Martinique, in the West Indies. vras terrific, houses. being blown down, crops destroy, and many persons killed and injured. PARIS, FRIDAY.-4tis only now that thafull magnitude of the terrible disaster at Martinique is. beginning to appear. The latest official despatche3,--bring up the number of lives lost to 218. This, however, only repre- sents the number of.persons who have •perished at the coast towns and villages' and it is thought the death roll will be even higher as it becomes possible :to communi- cate with the interior. An immense number were in- limed by falling buildings, trees, and stones. All over the Island houses-were completely demolished by the violence of the hurricane. At Ducos, a town near the west coast, not far ftem Fort Royal, only four dwellings remain intact. The- greater portion of the population are without shelter or food, and in the brief but expres- sive language of the official telegram, general consterna- tion prevails.

div.head: SHIP CANAL.
div.p: THE SHIP CANAL.
FATAL ACCIDENT NEAR RUNCORN.

On Saturday as Ship Canal labourer, named Edward Dooney, 20 years of age, and lodging in Percy-street, Runcorn. died at the Ship Canal Eisspital, Latchford, . from injuries received the previous day whilst following his employment in.the "Big Field,". a part of the Run, corn section. It appears that a locomotive, called the Didsbury, had shunted a nambew of wagons to be emptied, and after this had been done, deceased jumped. into one of the wagons before it had, been fastened after tipping. Shortlyi after doing so theengine started, with the result that, the wagon again lipped, and deceased was thrown with his neck on the line and run over. He was immediateiyi conveyed to the. Latchford Hospital,, but died on the way.—On Monday. afternoon an inquest was held on ths.body, before tirt,..lll C. Yates, aunty.c coroner.—Richard Pike said thiat be shouted "Right:: away" meaning that as far as, he, was concerned, the engine drivn could start the train but it appears that the roper should have given the signal that all wria, right before the engehe driver started. When he,(pike)' I shouted Right away" the engine driver started the. train, but found that all the wagons were not fastened 4. with the result that the unfastened wagon, in which de— ceased was, „again tipped, andthrew him on the line.— Edward Cox,..theengine driver4.stated that he heard the shout "Right away," and ; supposing all was right started the •engine. The rep? runner was at the. time away at other work.—The •jllr7 returned a verdict of " Accidental death." At the •sate time, a censure was, passed upon, the engine driver fur his negligence in not seeing that. the wagons were coupled beforestartinuk,

RUNCORN IMPROVEMENT ACT, 1852. ELECTION OF COMMISSIONERS. NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a MEETING of persons entitled to vote at the Election of Com- missioners under the above named Act will be held IN THE MARKET HILL, BRIDGE-ST., RUNCORN, ON THURSDAY TUB 3RD DAY OF SEPTEMBER, 1891, for the Election of six commissioners in the place of Mr. James Pritchard, Mr. John W. Lightburn, Mr. William Mellor, Mr Edwin Imison, Mr, James Dobson, and Mr. William R. Wass, who then retire from office but are eligible for re-elect ion. RESISTING THE Potics.—A young man named John Barber pleaded guilty to having on the 15th inst. resisted P.C. Hodgkinson while iu She execution of his duty, and he was lined 10s. and costs 8s: 6d. Rossixa A GWOCER.—John Campbell, a youth, and John Ryan, a Ship Canal labourer, were charged with stealing 41bs. of cheese worth 2s. Bd., from the shop door of Walter Collier, grocer and provision dealer, Church-st.—Campbell said Ryan told him he had bought the cheese and asked him to take it along to his" lodge" at the Model. Ryan denied this statement and said Campbell had had tw3 glasses of ale with him and he said he would take the piece of cheese. Be .(Ryan) tried to persuade him not to do so.—Campbell was fined ss. or 'I days' hard labour. Ryan was discharged. WIDNES POLICE COURT. MONDAY.—Before Mr. F. H. Gossage and Mr. H. Wade- Deacon. DEUNKENIgESS.—For this offence a fine of ss. and costs was imposed upon John Corker, Joseph Harrison, Eliza- brth Jones, Mary Muldoon, and Isaiah Eatock.—Mary J. Riley made her 25th appearance and was fined 10s. and costs. or 14 days. BEGGING.—Henry Oldham, a tramp, was sentenced to 14 days' hard labour for begging. BLEEPING OUT.—John Molyneux„ J. M. Creese, and John Dagnall, were sentenced to seven days' hard labour for sleeping out. ASSAULT ON THE Num—Hugh Simon, of Crouton, was charged with being drunk at Rainhill and assaulting P.C. Palmer by kicking him.—He was fined ss. and costs on each charge. A PICEPOCERT.—John Doyle, who said he came from Burnley, was charged with attempting to pick pockets on Widnes Market Ground on Saturday night.—Mrs. Arch, Vine-st., and Mrs. Tweddall, wife.of a constable, gave evidence that the prisoner attempted to pick their pockets, and P.C. McCracker said he watched the pri- soner and saw him attempt to pick several pockets.—The prisoner who denied the charge was sentenced to 14 days' hard labour. TUESDAY.—Before Mr. T. S. Timmis. DRUNEENNESS.—Sarah A.. McGee, William McDonough, and Alice Rimmer, were each fined ss. and costs for drunkenness.
